Attached is a short p95 snapshot and a few stack traces from our client side. Please advise immediate mitigation steps and ETA for a fix. This is production traffic for our checkout flows.

Subject: RE: High 5xx/429 after model variant update - urgent

Initial triage: we see a sharp increase in per-request runtime for model v2.3-q on the dedicated pool serving Acme (GPU pool id: d-pool-42). Kernel telemetry shows higher KV cache miss rate for the quantized execution path at the sequence lengths Acme uses. That leads to CPU/GPU stalls and request queuing -> increased request timeouts and client retries, which then produce 429s from our admission control.

Short-term mitigations I can apply immediately (need ack):
- Route Acme traffic to the unquantized v2.3 (non-q) variant for their dedicated pool (fall back).
- Open temporary burst nodes for d-pool-42 (scale up GPU count by +25%) to flatten queueing while rollback happens.
- Disable model-level client-side retries via routing policy for Acme (prevent retry storm).

I've uploaded compressed serving traces and logs to the folder; attaching reference: serving-logs-acme-20260701.zip. I'm starting the fallback route now; will confirm within 30 minutes.

-- Markus
Markus Klein
SRE Lead, Serving Runtime
Attachments: serving-logs-acme-20260701.zip

Sam — thanks for the quick report and data. We are treating this as a P1 for Acme. Our engineering team is proposing a targeted rollback/fallback to the non-quantized variant and a temporary capacity increase while we investigate the quantized kernel mismatch.

Proposed immediate steps:
- Proceed with fallback routing for Acme (we will not change global traffic).
- If fallback does not stabilize within 30–45 min, we'll perform a controlled rollback of v2.3-q for Acme's dedicated pool and keep you updated on timing.
- We will offer a service credit for the affected window; I will confirm amount after we have an SLO impact calc.

Would you like a short call now to confirm the plan?

—Marissa

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>

Subject: Exec summary and ask: Acme P1 (decision needed)

Quick summary for execs: Acme (dedicated pool d-pool-42) experienced a 5xx/429 surge after yesterday's rollout of v2.3-q quantized variant. Cause: kernel/quantization path mismatch at observed sequence lengths leading to cache misses and queued requests -> retry storms. Impact: checkout latency and order throughput impacted; customer requests rollback/fallback and credits.

Decisions needed:
1) Approve immediate tenant-level rollback to non-quantized variant for Acme if fallback routing does not normalize within 45 minutes (engineering estimate).
2) Approve up to a 15% service credit for the incident window if customer demand is high (Marissa to propose exact amount after SLO calc).
3) Approve cross-team RCA priority (post-mortem within 72 hours) and a code freeze on quantized kernel changes until patch validated.

Markus/Rishi — status update and ETA?

Hannah
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 1 Jul 2026 14:45:00 -0700
Subject: RE: High 5xx/429 after model variant update - urgent

Update: fallback routing to non-quantized v2.3 has been applied for Acme at 14:11 PDT. We rolled additional burst nodes and disabled client-side retry in routing policy. Error rates dropped from 9.4% 5xx/429 to 0.6% over the 20-minute window; P95 returned to ~210ms. I triggered a controlled rollback of v2.3-q for d-pool-42 and am running canaries on unquantized execution.

Next steps: RCA scheduled for 2026-07-02 09:00 PDT with Serving, Runtime, and SRE. Follow-up: confirm SLO impact and finalize credit proposal.
